proposal.comment: [Playbook] The Agreement has no indemnification section at all, even though Sections 9.3, 19.4, 21.3 and 30.5 assume one exists (9.3 cross-references "Section 20.5"). We have added the standard Vendor indemnity for third-party IP claims, breach of law, Vendor-caused data breach and wilful misconduct, with usual exclusions and remedies, plus a reciprocal but narrow Customer indemnity.

ops.text: 20.1 Vendor shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Customer and its Affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, liabilities, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (a) an allegation that the Services, Deliverables or Vendor Technology infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right; (b) Vendor's breach of Applicable Law; (c) any unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor; or (d) Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct. 20.2 Vendor's obligation under Section 20.1(a) does not apply to the extent a claim arises from Customer's modification of the Services or Deliverables without Vendor's authorization, combination with items not supplied or recommended by Vendor, or Vendor's compliance with Customer's written specifications. 20.3 Customer shall indemnify Vendor against third-party claims to the extent arising out of content Customer provides to the Services in breach of this Agreement or Customer's breach of Applicable Law. 20.4 The indemnified Party shall give the indemnifying Party prompt written notice of the claim (delay does not excuse the indemnity except to the extent of resulting prejudice), the indemnifying Party shall control the defence with counsel reasonably acceptable to the indemnified Party, and the indemnified Party shall provide reasonable cooperation at the indemnifying Party's expense and may participate with its own counsel at its own cost. No settlement imposing a non-indemnified obligation or admission on the indemnified Party may be made without its consent. 20.5 If a claim under Section 20.1(a) arises or is reasonably likely, Vendor shall, at its expense, procure the necessary rights, or modify or replace the affected item with a functionally equivalent non-infringing item. If Vendor cannot do so within a reasonable period, Customer may terminate the affected Services or Deliverables and receive a refund of Fees paid for them, including prepaid Fees for the terminated period.

quote: 21.1 Except for Excluded Claims, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of the Fees paid or payable by Customer during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim and USD 1,000,000. The cap is mutual and applies regardless of the form of action or number of claims.
rationale: Section 21 meets our preferred position in full. The cap is expressly mutual and set at the greater of Fees "paid or payable" by Customer in the twelve months preceding the event and USD 1,000,000 (21.1). Section 21.2 is a mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages, and it helpfully confirms that data restoration, replacement services, notification and incident-response costs are direct damages. Section 21.3 places outside the cap exactly the carve-outs we require — breach of confidentiality, data-protection or security obligations, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, and infringement of the other Party's IP — and confirms Customer's obligation to pay undisputed Fees is not "damages" subject to the cap. Section 21.4 preserves each cap and exclusion independently and on failure of an exclusive remedy, and 18.2 confirms insurance does not limit Vendor's liabilities. The "Fees" definition (1.5) covers recurring subscription, professional services and usage fees, so the cap base is substantive (not an illusory set-up fee); it excludes a one-time implementation charge, which is immaterial given the USD 1,000,000 floor. No hidden cap or one-sided liability language appears in the warranty or indemnity provisions. No redline required.

rationale: Section 7.2 imposes the MFN on us, not the Vendor: we must disclose and match for Vendor "any more favourable commercial offer" we receive, with no product limitation, no time limit and no comparison carve-outs. quote: 19.2 For ninety days after delivery or acceptance, whichever is later, each Deliverable will materially conform to its documentation and acceptance criteria. Hosted Services will conform throughout the subscription term. Vendor warrants it has authority to enter the Agreement and grant the rights stated here.
rationale: Compliant at the preferred position; no redline and no counterparty comment proposed. (1) Duration: 19.2 warrants Deliverable conformity for ninety days - i.e. 90 days, three months - measured from the later of delivery or acceptance, and hosted Services must conform throughout the subscription term. The 90-day Deliverable period meets the preferred services/deliverable standard, and the term-long hosted-Services warranty satisfies the preferred software-conformance requirement (it runs for as long as Customer subscribes rather than a fixed 12-month window). The automated period check failed only because the document spells the number out as "ninety days" instead of "90" or "ninety (90)"; that is a drafting-style artifact, not a shortfall below the 90-day threshold, so it is noted here as internal evidence rather than raised as a negotiation issue. (2) Standard of performance: 19.1 warrants Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner by qualified personnel in accordance with industry standards, the Agreement and each Order Form, plus material conformity of Services and Deliverables to documentation and agreed specifications. (3) Remedy: 19.4 tracks the model remedy - prompt re-performance, repair or replacement at no charge, and if Vendor cannot cure within a reasonable period, termination of the affected item and refund of Fees paid for it - and is expressly non-exclusive for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security and indemnified claims. (4) Additional warranties: 19.3 covers malicious code intentionally introduced by Vendor, compliance with Applicable Law, no material diminution of functionality, and no contaminating open-source use. (5) Disclaimer: no "AS IS" language appears anywhere in the Agreement; 19.5 is confined to implied warranties and expressly provides that no disclaimer limits an express warranty, service level, indemnity, confidentiality duty, data-protection duty or stated remedy, so the disclaimer does not swallow the express warranties and walk-away territory is not implicated. Section 6.2 supplies a further refund right after two failed correction cycles.
